data.description:
The September 18 collection read all 29 public listing pages without following shortener destinations. It contains 1,448 displayed rows and 1,364 unique aliases. A task-family review retained 375 aliases: 75 already in the published baseline and 300 additional candidates, representing 262 distinct destinations. Families include New York school enrollment, MAX.gov/USAspending, CBS and Project Arclight. These numbers count alias identities, not verified AI messages, unique information, agents or attacks. Individual creation times are not established by the listing snapshot. Generic tests were excluded; some task-family assignments remain heuristic.

Internal company attribution review (2026-09-28): OpenAI — moderate at collection level confidence. This collection overlaps the published OpenAI-linked activity: 75 aliases are already in that baseline, and the additional candidates continue specific retrieval-task families; OAI-labelled aliases provide another contextual clue. OpenAI is therefore the working company label for the collection. The 300 additional candidates are not individually authenticated, and this label does not imply that every alias has the same author or provider. This label is an internal attribution hypothesis, not a confirmed attribution or a publication-ready conclusion.
data.summary: A reviewed Popcat inventory found 300 additional task-associated aliases beyond 75 already published aliases. The new aliases cover 262 destinations, including data-retrieval proxy chains. These are candidate entries, not 300 verified agents or attacks.
